mechanism: A VAE compresses raw observations into compact spatial latent vectors (z); an MDN-RNN learns to predict future latent states given current z and action, capturing temporal dynamics. A small controller C acts solely on these compressed representations. Because C operates on rich abstractions rather than raw pixels, it requires far fewer parameters. Crucially, C can be trained entirely within dream rollouts generated by the RNN, then transferred to the real environment, since the world model approximates environment dynamics.
invariant: Separating perception (spatial compression), prediction (temporal modeling), and control (compact policy on latent features) reduces the parameter complexity required of the controller, independent of the specific environment or task.
prediction: A controller trained exclusively on hallucinated dream rollouts generated by the world model will achieve performance in the real environment comparable to or exceeding a controller trained directly on real environment interactions with equivalent interaction budgets.
failure_mode: When the agent's policy systematically exploits regions of the dream distribution that do not correspond to real environment dynamics—i.e., the world model's learned distribution diverges from reality—the dream-trained policy transfers poorly or fails entirely in the actual environment.
source_excerpt: We can even train our agent entirely inside of its own hallucinated dream generated by its world model, and transfer this policy back into the actual environment.
